backups.title: Backups
backups.subtitle: Full and incremental backups of the app to FTP, FTPS, SFTP or SCP, with restore from the remote location.
backups.empty_text: Add a location such as your NAS or a storage box. The app then makes a full backup weekly and incremental ones in between.
backups.delete_confirm: Remove backup location {{name}}? Backups already on it stay there.
backups.name: Name
backups.ftp_warning: Plain FTP sends your password unencrypted. Use FTPS or SFTP where you can, and turn on backup encryption.
backups.ftps_implicit_hint: Usually port 990. Off means explicit TLS (AUTH TLS) on port 21.
backups.verify_tls_hint: Turn off only for self-signed certificates on your own network.
backups.encryption_hint: Backups are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they leave the server. Keep this passphrase safe: without it a backup can't be restored.
backups.cron_hint: Times in UTC. Empty = not scheduled.
backups.keep_full_hint: Older chains are removed after a new full backup.
backups.restore_subtitle: These backups are on the remote location. Incremental backups are restored together with their full backup.
backups.remote_empty: No backups found on this location.
backups.restore_warning: Users, settings and history go back to {{date}}. A safety copy of the current database is made first and put back if the restore fails.

mail.security_tls_hint: SMTPS: TLS from the first byte, usually port 465.
mail.security_none_hint: Only for a relay on your own network.
mail.username_hint: Leave empty for a relay without authentication.
mail.verify_tls_hint: Checks the server certificate and host name.
mail.no_tls_warning: Without TLS, passwords and emails travel unencrypted.
mail.dkim_hint: Sign outgoing mail so receivers can verify it really comes from your domain.
mail.dkim_key_hint: RSA or Ed25519 key in PEM format. Publish the public key at <selector>._domainkey.<domain>.
mail.test_hint: Uses the values in the form, also before you save them.

web.title: Web server & proxy
web.subtitle: How the app is reached: directly with its own HTTPS, or behind a reverse proxy such as Zoraxy.
web.mode_proxy_hint: The proxy handles HTTPS. Nginx listens on plain HTTP and trusts X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto only from the addresses below.
web.mode_direct_hint: Nginx serves HTTPS itself on port 443 and redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
web.trusted_proxies_hint: IP address or range of Zoraxy, one per line, e.g. 10.10.4.2 or 10.10.4.0/24.
web.restrict: Only accept traffic from the proxy
web.restrict_hint: Blocks direct access that bypasses Zoraxy.
web.cert_hint: Default is a self-signed certificate. For Let's Encrypt run certbot on the server and enter its paths here.
web.base_path_hint: / for the root, or e.g. /mmn to serve the app at https://host/mmn.
web.dev_note: On a development machine the settings are saved, but Nginx is configured only on an installed server.
web.apply_failed: Applying failed; the previous configuration is still active
web.not_https: The app sees this request as plain HTTP. Check that the proxy address is correct and that Zoraxy sends X-Forwarded-Proto.
web.zoraxy_1: In Zoraxy, add an HTTP proxy rule for your host name, e.g. mcp.example.com.
web.zoraxy_2: Target: the IP of this server on port 80 (Zoraxy connected from {{ip}}).
web.zoraxy_3: Turn on TLS/HTTPS with a certificate for the host name (Zoraxy can request one via ACME).
web.zoraxy_4: Leave WebSocket support on and do not strip headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, Host).
web.zoraxy_5: Enter Zoraxy's IP address above and set the public address under General.

help.subtitle: How things work, and how to connect an AI.
help.topic_mcp_text: Step by step: let an AI app work with this server through the built-in MCP server.
help.topic_backups_text: A full backup stores everything; incremental backups store only what changed since. A restore takes the full backup plus the incrementals up to the moment you pick.

mcphelp.title: Connect an AI to the MCP server
mcphelp.subtitle: Let Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot answer questions about this server and carry out tasks. You decide what each app may do.
mcphelp.local_title: Cloud AI apps need a public HTTPS address
mcphelp.local_text: Claude (web and app) and ChatGPT connect from their own cloud, so they can't reach a local or plain-HTTP address. Publish the app through Zoraxy with a domain and certificate and set the public address under General. Claude Code and VS Code run on your own computer and also work on your local network.
mcphelp.claude_desc: Add it once as a custom connector; it then works in every chat.
mcphelp.claude_2: Click Add custom connector and give it a name, e.g. MCP Management Node.
mcphelp.claude_4: Click Add and then Connect. You're sent to this app: sign in, pick the permissions and click Allow access.

mcphelp.claude_desktop_token_text: Create an API token, then add this to <c>claude_desktop_config.json</c> (Settings → Developer → Edit config). It needs Node.js on your computer.
mcphelp.cc_desc: Claude in your terminal. Runs on your own computer, so a local address works too.
mcphelp.cc_2: Start Claude Code, type /mcp, choose mcp-node and then Authenticate.
mcphelp.cc_3: Your browser opens this app: sign in and click Allow access. Done.
mcphelp.with_token: With an API token instead of OAuth
mcphelp.with_token_text: Create a token under API tokens and pass it as a header:
mcphelp.chatgpt_desc: Via developer mode, available in ChatGPT's paid plans.
mcphelp.chatgpt_1: Open Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and turn on Developer mode.
mcphelp.chatgpt_2: Go back to Apps & Connectors and click Create.
mcphelp.chatgpt_3: Give it a name and enter the MCP Server URL:
mcphelp.chatgpt_4: Choose OAuth as authentication, tick that you trust the application and click Create.
mcphelp.chatgpt_5: Sign in to this app in the window that opens, pick the permissions and click Allow access. In a chat, add the connector via + → Developer mode.
mcphelp.chatgpt_note: ChatGPT asks for your confirmation before it runs a tool that changes something.
mcphelp.copilot_desc: Use the tools in Copilot's agent mode.
mcphelp.copilot_1: Create .vscode/mcp.json in your project (or run MCP: Add Server from the command palette):
mcphelp.copilot_2: Click Start above the server in mcp.json. VS Code asks you to sign in: allow it, approve in this app and click Allow access.
mcphelp.copilot_3: Open Copilot Chat, switch to Agent mode and check under the tools icon that mcp-node is on.
mcphelp.copilot_4: For Copilot Business or Enterprise, an admin must allow MCP servers in Copilot in the organisation policy.
mcphelp.copilot_token_text: Prefer a token? VS Code asks for it once and stores it securely:
mcphelp.other_desc: The server follows the MCP standard.
mcphelp.other_1: Transport: Streamable HTTP at the address above (JSON responses, stateless).
mcphelp.other_2: OAuth 2.1: discovery at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, dynamic client registration and PKCE.
mcphelp.other_3: Or a token: header Authorization: Bearer mmn_… from the API tokens page.
mcphelp.safety_1: Each AI app gets only the permissions you tick; read-only is the default.
mcphelp.safety_2: Destructive actions such as a restore or an update require the AI to confirm the exact target.
mcphelp.safety_3: Every call is in the AI activity log: which app, which token, parameters, result and duration.
mcphelp.safety_4: Disconnect an app or revoke a token and it loses access immediately.

agents.title: Agents & pairing
agents.subtitle: How agents on your nodes reach this app.
agents.endpoint_desc: Agents keep one outgoing connection (mutual TLS) to this address.
agents.address_hint: Host name or IP the nodes can reach. Empty: the host of the public address (General).
agents.nginx_queued: Nginx is being reconfigured for the new port.
agents.auto_update_hint: When an agent connects with another version than {{version}} (the one shipped with this app), it is updated.
agents.check_hours_hint: Agents also check by themselves every 6 hours.

agents.zoraxy_1: Agents use mutual TLS, which Nginx on this server checks itself. In Zoraxy add a Stream Proxy (TCP) from port {{port}} to this server's port {{port}}, not an HTTP rule.

nodeshelp.title: Connect a Proxmox node
nodeshelp.subtitle: One command per node; the connection is always started by the node.
nodeshelp.step_1: Open Proxmox › Nodes and click Add node. Pick the environment (Home or a customer).
nodeshelp.step_2: Copy the command and run it as root on the node (shell in the Proxmox web UI or SSH). It downloads the agent package, checks its SHA-256 and installs it.
nodeshelp.step_3: The agent creates its own key and pairs with the one-time code. It checks that it talks to this app with the CA fingerprint in the command.
nodeshelp.step_4: Within seconds the node appears with its status, metrics and pending updates.
nodeshelp.step_5: Set the notification mail of the environment and the CPU power mode per node. Both are applied by the agent, also after reboots.
nodeshelp.network_1: Nodes connect out to port 8443 of this app. At customer sites nothing has to be opened.
nodeshelp.network_2: Behind Zoraxy use a Stream Proxy (TCP) for that port, see Administration › Agents & pairing.
nodeshelp.security_text: Mutual TLS with a certificate per node, issued by this app's own CA. Removing a node in the app blocks its certificate immediately.
nodeshelp.files: On the node: /etc/mmn-agent (certificates), /var/lib/mmn-agent (state), service mmn-agent. Logs: journalctl -u mmn-agent.

mcpcaps.title: What the MCP can do
mcpcaps.subtitle: Ask an AI about your servers and let it do the work, with every step on record.
mcpcaps.idea_title: One agent per server instead of a remote session everywhere
mcpcaps.idea_1: The idea: you install a small agent on each Proxmox node, Linux and Windows server once. Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot then talks only to this app through MCP, and the app reaches the servers through their agents. No separate remote sessions per machine, no screen sessions to keep open.
mcpcaps.idea_2: So you can simply ask “is mail working on www1?” or “which servers are affected by this nginx CVE?”. The AI looks up statuses and logs, explains what it finds and, when you allow it, fixes things. Every question and every action, with its parameters and result, ends up in the AI activity log.
mcpcaps.now_system_desc: Version, update status, channel, installing updates.
mcpcaps.now_backups_desc: Locations, history, starting a backup, restoring one.
mcpcaps.now_mail_desc: Check and change the SMTP settings, send a test email.
mcpcaps.now_audit_desc: What changed, by whom, from the interface or via AI.
mcpcaps.next_intro: Each phase adds its tools to the same MCP server. You choose per connection (and later per environment) what an AI may do.
mcpcaps.ask_desc: Examples of what you can ask.
mcpcaps.ask_1: Did all backups succeed this week?
mcpcaps.ask_2: Is there an update for MCP Management Node, and what changes?
mcpcaps.ask_3: Send me a test email to check the mail settings.
mcpcaps.ask_4: I think mail on www1 isn't working. Can you check?
mcpcaps.ask_5: There's a CVE for nginx. Which of my servers run an affected version?
mcpcaps.ask_6: Search the logs on db2 for errors from the last hour.
mcpcaps.ask_7: What's the update status of all servers and nodes?
mcpcaps.trail_1: Every call is logged: which AI app, which user or token, which tool, the parameters, the result and how long it took.
mcpcaps.trail_2: Commands that run on a server are logged with their reason, exit code and output.
mcpcaps.trail_3: Read-only is the default; changes need a permission you grant, and destructive actions need explicit confirmation.
mcpcaps.trail_4: Disconnect an AI app or revoke a token and it loses access immediately.
mcpcaps.now_proxmox_desc: Status, CPU, memory, disk and guests; environments, pairing, CPU governor and notification mail.
mcpcaps.now_node_updates_desc: Pending updates per node, installing them as a job, rebooting with confirmation.
mcpcaps.now_servers_desc: Journal and event log, services, installed software, files and commands (bash or PowerShell) on Proxmox nodes, Linux and Windows servers.
mcpcaps.now_guests_desc: List, start and stop guests, snapshots and rollback, migration, resources, creating containers and VMs.
mcpcaps.now_library_desc: The template library and its sync, and installing community scripts (after reviewing them).
mcpcaps.now_tasks_desc: Create, change and start scheduled maintenance, and read the reports.
mcpcaps.ask_9: Do an apt upgrade in all containers tonight, with a snapshot first.
mcpcaps.ask_10: Create a Debian 13 container for Nginx on the least loaded node.
mcpcaps.now_network_desc: Bridges and VLANs per guest, the firewall, SDN designs and config backups. Changes start with a dry run.
mcpcaps.now_cluster_desc: HA resources and rules, replication, Proxmox backup jobs and storage.
mcpcaps.now_monitoring_desc: CPU, memory and disk trends per node, alerts and SMART data.
mcpcaps.now_deploy_desc: Deploy GitHub repositories into containers, with a snapshot first.
mcpcaps.now_troubleshoot_desc: Health checks, log search on many servers at once, error overviews and CVE checks.
mcpcaps.now_copy_desc: Copy folders between servers through the agents, with a reason in the log.
mcpcaps.scen_intro: What the AI does when you ask something. You see every step afterwards in the AI activity log.
mcpcaps.scen_mail_a: Runs a health check on www1, checks postfix/dovecot, searches the mail log for rejects and timeouts, explains the cause and, if you allow it, restarts the service.
mcpcaps.scen_cve_q: There's a CVE for nginx, fixed in 1.26.3. Which servers are affected?
mcpcaps.scen_cve_a: Compares the installed nginx version on every server with 1.26.3, lists the affected ones and says whether a pending update fixes it. On request it installs that update.
mcpcaps.scen_updates_q: What's the update status of all servers?
mcpcaps.scen_updates_a: Lists pending updates and required reboots per Proxmox node, Linux and Windows server (apt, dnf or Windows Update).
mcpcaps.scen_windows_q: The print spooler on fs01 keeps stopping. Why?
mcpcaps.scen_windows_a: Reads the System event log on fs01 for the Service Control Manager, shows the error codes and the status of the service, and restarts it if you allow it.
mcpcaps.scen_copy_a: Starts a copy from agent to agent through this app, follows the progress and reports size and number of files. Owner and permissions are kept; the reason is logged.
mcpcaps.scen_errors_q: Something is wrong at customer X. Check all their servers.
mcpcaps.scen_errors_a: Looks for failed services, errors in the last hour, full disks and memory pressure on every server in that environment and summarises what needs attention.
mcpcaps.ask_11: Which Windows servers still need updates and a reboot?
mcpcaps.ask_12: Search the event log on dc01 for failed logons today.
mcpcaps.ask_13: Which switch port is www1 connected to?
mcpcaps.now_unifi_desc: Gateways, switches and APs of every customer, clients, WiFi and VLANs, firmware, events, WiFi troubleshooting and the guest isolation check.
mcpcaps.now_doors_desc: Doors and lock state, the access log, schedules, remote unlock and lock rules.
mcpcaps.scen_wifi_q: Why can't laptop-anna get on the WiFi?
mcpcaps.scen_wifi_a: Looks the laptop up by name or MAC, checks whether it is connected and where, its IP, the AP's state, and per SSID: WPA3-only, MAC filters, hidden name and blackout schedules. Explains the cause, e.g. that the MAC allow list refuses it.
mcpcaps.scen_firmware_q: Which access points need a firmware update?
mcpcaps.scen_firmware_a: Lists every AP (or switch, gateway) with a newer firmware version across all customers and consoles, with the current version and whether it is online.
mcpcaps.scen_guest_q: Is the guest network isolated from the LAN?
mcpcaps.scen_guest_a: Finds the guest networks and checks the zone-based firewall policies to each LAN network: isolated, partly (with the exceptions) or open, plus client isolation on the guest SSID.
mcpcaps.scen_door_q: Who opened the server room last night?
mcpcaps.scen_door_a: Reads the UniFi Access log for that door and time window and lists who opened it, when and how (badge, PIN, mobile or remote), including refused attempts.
mcpcaps.ask_14: Why can't the printer on the 2nd floor get on the WiFi?
mcpcaps.ask_15: Which UniFi devices need a firmware update?
mcpcaps.ask_16: Is the guest WiFi at customer A separated from the office network?
mcpcaps.ask_17: Who opened the server room last night?

console.title: Console
console.auth_failed: The console refused the password. Reconnect to get a new one.
console.single_use: This console session was already used or has expired. Start it again from the app.

gx.title: VMs & containers
gx.desc: All virtual machines and containers on your Proxmox VE nodes.
gx.create_desc: Choose where the new guest comes from. The node defaults to the least loaded one.
gx.empty_hint: Nodes report their guests every 20 seconds. Create one, or change the filters.
gx.list_hint: Click a guest for details, console and snapshots.
gx.not_found: This guest was not found. It may have been deleted or moved to another node.
gx.console_vnc: Screen of the VM via noVNC, with Ctrl+Alt+Del.
gx.console_term: Terminal of the container in the browser.
gx.console_not_running: Start the guest first to open its console.
gx.config_unavailable: The configuration could not be read right now.
gx.no_agent_ips: Install the QEMU guest agent to see IP addresses.
gx.resources_hint: Changes to running guests apply when the guest supports hot-plug, otherwise after a restart.
gx.onboot_hint: Start this guest when the node boots.
gx.snapshots_desc: Save the current state and go back to it later.
gx.snapshot_ram_hint: Also saves the memory, so a rollback continues where the VM was. Takes longer.
gx.rollback_text: Everything that changed after this snapshot is lost.
gx.rollback_start: Start the guest after the rollback
gx.migrate_live_hint: The VM keeps running during the move. Local disks are copied along.
gx.migrate_ct_restart: A running container is stopped, moved and started again (restart migration).
gx.migrate_hint: The guest stays in the same cluster and keeps its ID.
gx.migrate_no_cluster: Migration needs a Proxmox VE cluster with at least two nodes.
gx.destroy_text: The guest and all its disks are removed for good. Snapshots are lost too.
gx.destroy_type: Type the ID ({{vmid}}) or the name to confirm
gx.node_suggested: Suggested: the least loaded node (60% memory, 40% CPU).
gx.template_will_push: This template is not on the node yet. It is copied there first.
gx.no_templates: No templates: add them under CT templates
gx.nesting_hint: Needed for systemd and Docker inside the container.
gx.ssh_keys_hint: One per line. A password or a key is required.
gx.no_isos: No ISO images on this node
gx.windows_hint: For Windows you also need the VirtIO driver ISO during setup (disk and network drivers).
gx.cloud_hint: The image is downloaded on the node, imported as the boot disk and set up with cloud-init. The disk grows to the size you choose.

cs.intro: Ready-made installers from the Proxmox VE community scripts project. The list is synced every night.
cs.empty: The list is empty. Sync it first (the node or app needs internet access to GitHub).
cs.root_title: Runs as root on the node
cs.root_text: This script runs with full rights on the chosen Proxmox VE node. Read it before you continue: exactly this version (see sha256) runs.
cs.engine_hint: The script loads the shared helper functions of the project (build.func) at run time from the same repository.
cs.mode_default_hint: Runs unattended with the defaults of the script, plus the settings below. Follow the output live.
cs.mode_advanced_hint: Opens a terminal in the browser where you answer the questions of the script yourself.
cs.password_hint: Leave empty for automatic login on the console.
cs.reviewed_hint: Required: the app only runs the version that was shown to you.
cs.advanced_running: The script runs in the terminal below. Answer its questions; closing this window stops the script.
cs.advanced_log: The output is also saved as a job on the node.

tpl.title: CT templates
tpl.desc: One central library of container templates, kept up to date on every Proxmox VE node.
tpl.add_official_desc: Templates from the Proxmox VE appliance index (pveam).
tpl.custom_desc: Upload your own template (.tar.gz, .tar.xz or .tar.zst) or download it from a URL. It is stored in the app and included in backups.
tpl.catalog_never: The index has not been read yet. Refresh it (needs an online node).
tpl.drop: Drop a file here or click to choose one
tpl.url_hint: The app downloads the file and stores it in the library.
tpl.download_started: Download started, the template appears when it is done.
tpl.storage_hint: The storage on each node where templates are placed (it must allow the content type vztmpl).
tpl.storage_override_hint: Only for this template. Empty uses the default.
tpl.sync_on_hint: The nightly sync places this template on every node.
tpl.follow_latest_hint: When the index has a newer build, the library moves to it and nodes are updated.
tpl.remove_text: The template is removed from the library. Copies on the nodes stay where they are.
tpl.empty_hint: Add the official templates you use, such as Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04.
tpl.nightly_hint: Every night the scheduled task "Nightly template sync" brings all nodes up to date. Change it under Scheduled tasks.

tasks.title: Scheduled tasks
tasks.desc: Recurring maintenance on containers and nodes, with a snapshot first and a mailed report.
tasks.cron_hint: minute hour day month weekday, in time zone {{tz}}.
tasks.kind_ct_apt_upgrade_hint: Runs apt-get update and full-upgrade in each container (apk, dnf and pacman too).
tasks.kind_ct_community_update_hint: Runs the update of community-script containers (the /usr/bin/update command inside the container).
tasks.kind_node_updates_hint: Installs package updates on the Proxmox VE nodes. It does not reboot them.
tasks.kind_template_sync_hint: Brings all nodes up to date with the template library.
tasks.kind_custom_command_hint: Runs your own shell script in containers or on nodes, as root.
tasks.command_hint: Runs with bash. Exit code 99 means skipped.
tasks.exclude_hint: Container IDs to skip, separated by commas.
tasks.snapshot_hint: Takes a snapshot of each container before it starts.
tasks.rollback_hint: If the command fails, the container goes back to the snapshot.
tasks.parallel_hint: Targets on one node always run one after the other.
tasks.mail_to_hint: Comma separated. Empty uses the notification address from the mail settings.
tasks.remove_text: The task and its schedule are removed. Earlier runs stay in the history.
tasks.timezone_hint: All schedules use this time zone.
tasks.running_hint: Still running. This page updates by itself.

net.title: Network
net.desc: Bridges, VLANs, firewall and SDN across your Proxmox nodes. Changes are always previewed and can be rolled back.
net.no_bridges_hint: Connect a Proxmox node with the agent to see its bridges.
net.missing_bridge: Guests point to this bridge, but it doesn't exist on the node.
net.no_guests_on_bridge: No VMs or containers use this bridge.
net.ports_hint: Physical ports or bonds, separated by spaces. Leave empty for an internal bridge.
net.bridge_desc: Changes are staged first. Nothing changes on the node until you apply them.
net.cidr_hint: Leave empty for a bridge without an address on the host.
net.vlan_aware_hint: Lets guests use VLAN tags on this bridge.
net.stage_hint: Staged changes are only applied when you press Apply.
net.pending_desc: This is the difference with /etc/network/interfaces on the node.
net.apply_explain: The node reloads its network. If this app can't reach the node again within 90 seconds, the node restores the old configuration by itself. A backup is kept here too.
net.fw_cluster_desc: Applies to every node of the cluster.
net.fw_cluster_warning: Turning the cluster firewall on with policy DROP can lock you out. Make sure there is a rule that allows the web interface (8006) and SSH (22) first.
net.fw_guests_desc: VMs and containers on this node and whether their NICs use the firewall.
net.fw_guest_enable_hint: Rules only apply on NICs with the firewall option.
net.macro_hint: A ready-made rule, such as SSH or HTTPS. Leave empty to set the protocol and ports yourself.
net.sdn_designs_desc: Designs made in the SDN designer. Roll one out after reviewing the preview.
net.backups_desc: Copies of /etc/network/interfaces and the SDN configuration, made before every change.
net.restore_net_explain: The node gets this /etc/network/interfaces back and reloads its network, with the same 90 second safety net.
net.restore_sdn_explain: The SDN configuration of the cluster is replaced by this backup and reloaded on all nodes. The current configuration is backed up first.

sdn.title: SDN designer
sdn.desc: Design an SDN zone step by step and see what changes before it is rolled out to the nodes.
sdn.step_zone_hint: A zone is the network that ties the VNets together.
sdn.step_vnets_hint: Each VNet becomes a bridge that VMs and containers can use.
sdn.step_subnets_hint: Optional IP ranges, gateway and SNAT per VNet.
sdn.step_nodes_hint: On which nodes the zone becomes available.
sdn.step_review_hint: Check every change before rolling it out.
sdn.id_hint: 2 to 8 lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter.
sdn.type_vlan_hint: Tags traffic with a VLAN ID on an existing bridge. The most common choice.
sdn.type_simple_hint: An isolated bridge on each node, optionally with NAT and DHCP. No physical network needed.
sdn.type_vxlan_hint: A layer 2 overlay between nodes over UDP. Needs an MTU of 1450 or lower.
sdn.type_evpn_hint: VXLAN with BGP EVPN routing. Needs an EVPN controller.
sdn.type_qinq_hint: Stacks a customer VLAN inside a service VLAN.
sdn.peers_hint: IP addresses of all nodes, separated by commas.
sdn.ipam_hint: Proxmox keeps track of the IP addresses in the subnets.
sdn.dhcp_hint: Hand out addresses with dnsmasq. Install dnsmasq on the nodes first.
sdn.vnet_vlanaware: Allow VLAN tags inside this VNet
sdn.no_subnets: No subnets. That's fine for a plain layer 2 network.
sdn.all_nodes_hint: The zone is available on every node of the cluster, also nodes added later.
sdn.nodes_from_plan: The node list appears once the zone has a valid ID.
sdn.review_need_zone: Give the zone a valid ID first.
sdn.in_sync: The cluster already matches this design. Nothing to roll out.
sdn.review_intro: These changes will be made on cluster {{cluster}}:
sdn.review_safety: Before the rollout the current SDN configuration is backed up. If the reload fails it is restored automatically, and you can roll back by hand from Config backups.
sdn.rollback_hint: Not happy with the result? Roll back from
sdn.confirm_explain_one: {{count}} change is made and SDN is reloaded on the nodes. Guests on changed VNets can briefly lose their network.
sdn.confirm_explain_other: {{count}} changes are made and SDN is reloaded on the nodes. Guests on changed VNets can briefly lose their network.
sdn.preview_hint: Updates while you type. Compared with what is live on the cluster.

cl.title: Cluster & HA
cl.desc: High availability, replication, Proxmox backup jobs and storage.
cl.no_nodes_hint: Connect a Proxmox node with the agent first.
cl.ha_resources_hint: Guests that are restarted on another node when their node fails.
cl.ha_rules_hint: Which nodes a guest prefers, or which guests run together or apart.
cl.ha_groups_hint: Which nodes guests may run on, with a priority.
cl.replication_hint: Copies guest disks to another node on a schedule (ZFS only).
cl.replication_zfs: Replication works with guests on local ZFS storage only.
cl.schedule_hint: Proxmox calendar format, such as */15 or 02:30.
cl.backup_hint: The backup jobs of the Proxmox cluster itself (vzdump).
cl.backup_schedule_hint: For example: sun 01:00, daily 02:30 or mon..fri 22:00.
cl.storage_hint: Storage defined in the cluster, with usage seen from this node.
cl.storage_nodes_hint: Leave everything off to make it available on all nodes.

mon.title: Monitoring
mon.desc: CPU, memory and disks of every connected node, with trends and alerts.
mon.nodes_hint: Click a node for its trends, storage and disk health.
mon.no_nodes_hint: Connect a node with the agent to start collecting metrics.
mon.no_health: No data yet. It is collected every 10 minutes.
mon.alert_history_hint: The last 50 alerts. Alerts close by themselves when the value is back to normal.
mon.settings_hint: When an alert opens or closes, a mail is sent to the addresses below.
mon.mail_to_hint: Separate addresses with commas. Uses the mail server from Settings.
mon.th_smart: Alert on SMART errors and worn disks
mon.th_wearout_hint: For SSDs: life left as reported by SMART.
mon.th_unifi_hint: Alert when a UniFi device is offline or a UniFi connection can't be reached.

dep.title: Deployments
dep.desc: Deploy your GitHub repositories into containers, natively on Debian 13 without Docker.
dep.dialog_hint: The code is cloned into the container and your deploy command is run there.
dep.container_hint: An LXC container. Need a new one? Use Create → GitHub on the guests page.
dep.empty_hint: Connect GitHub and add a deployment, or create a new container from a repo.
dep.name: Name
dep.path_hint: Where the code is placed, such as /opt/myapp.
dep.setup_cmd_hint: Runs once on the first deployment, or when you ask for it. Use it to install packages.
dep.deploy_cmd_hint: Runs in the code folder on every deployment, as root.
dep.service_hint: Restarted after a successful deployment. Optional.
dep.env_hint: One KEY=value per line. Stored encrypted and written to /etc/mmn-deploy/<name>.env in the container.
dep.auto_off_hint: Only deploy when you press Deploy now, or via MCP.
dep.auto_webhook_hint: GitHub calls this app on every push. This app must be reachable from the internet.
dep.auto_poll_hint: This app checks the branch for new commits every 5 minutes. Works behind a firewall.
dep.snapshot_hint: Takes a container snapshot before deploying. The newest 3 are kept.
dep.rollback_hint: Restores the snapshot when the deployment fails.
dep.gh_hint: Add a fine-grained personal access token with read access to Contents and Metadata of your repositories.
dep.gh_token_hint: Stored encrypted. It is used inside containers only while cloning, never shown in logs.
dep.gh_needed: Connect GitHub first to deploy from your repositories.
dep.run_setup_hint: For the next deployment you start here.
dep.delete_hint: Only removes the deployment here. The container and its files stay.
dep.webhook_hint: Add this in GitHub under Settings → Webhooks.
dep.webhook_steps: Content type application/json, only the push event. Pushes to the selected branch start a deployment.
dep.with_ct_hint: Creates a new container and deploys the repository into it as soon as it runs. Debian 13 is chosen when it's in the library.

srv.title: Servers
srv.subtitle: Stand-alone Linux and Windows machines, managed by the same agent as the Proxmox nodes.
srv.k_attention_hint: Failed services, full disks, memory or a pending reboot
srv.list_desc: Click a server for services, logs, health, software, updates and a shell.
srv.empty_text: Install the agent on a Linux or Windows server with a one-time pairing code. It connects out to this app, so nothing has to be opened on the server.
srv.claude_note: Connect Claude (or another MCP client) under AI › Connections. It reaches every server through its agent; every step it takes is in the AI activity log.
srv.ask_2: There's a CVE for nginx, which servers are affected?
srv.ask_3: What's the update status of all servers?
srv.ask_4: Search all servers for errors from the last hour.
srv.ask_s1: Run a health check on {{name}} and explain what you find.
srv.ask_s2: Why did a service on {{name}} fail? Check the journal.
srv.ask_s2_win: Check the System event log on {{name}} for errors since this morning.
srv.ask_s3: Install the pending updates on {{name}} tonight.
srv.add_desc: Create a one-time pairing code and run one command on the server.
srv.add_how_linux: Works on Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL/Rocky/Alma, Fedora, SUSE and Alpine. On Debian and Ubuntu the .deb is installed; elsewhere the agent is placed in /usr/local/bin with a systemd service.
srv.add_how_win: Works on Windows Server 2016 and newer and Windows 10/11. The agent installs as a Windows service (MSI) and connects out to this app.
srv.run_linux: Run as root on the server
srv.linux_note: The script checks the SHA-256 of the download, installs the agent and pairs it with the code. The code works once.
srv.win_note: Downloads the MSI, checks its SHA-256 and installs the service. The server appears within seconds.
srv.win_msiexec_text: Download the MSI from this app and install it silently with these properties:
srv.logs_subtitle: Search the journal, Windows event logs or log files on many servers at once.
srv.paths_hint: Absolute paths, wildcards allowed, separated by commas. Newest files are searched first; .gz files too.
srv.unit_hint: A systemd unit or an event log provider. Leave empty for all.
srv.truncated: More results than shown. Narrow the search or the period.
srv.errors_desc: Failed services, errors in the journal or event log and other warning signs, per server.
srv.sw_subtitle: Which servers run a package, in which version, and are they affected by a vulnerability?
srv.sw_package_hint: Name or wildcard: nginx*, openssl, *7-zip*. On Windows also hotfixes: KB5*.
srv.sw_fixed_hint: From the advisory. Older versions are marked as affected.
srv.sw_no_fixed: Enter a fixed version to compare
srv.sw_installed_desc: Search packages (Linux) or installed programs and hotfixes (Windows).
srv.copy_subtitle: Copy folders or files from one server to another, directly through the agents.
srv.copy_dest_hint: Absolute path on the target; created if it doesn't exist.
srv.copy_overwrite_hint: Off: the copy stops if a file already exists.
srv.copy_note: Owner, permissions and timestamps are kept. Every copy is in the audit log.
srv.copy_how: The source agent packs the paths into a compressed archive and uploads it to this app over its own mTLS connection. The target agent then downloads and unpacks it. The servers don't need to reach each other, so this also works between customer sites. The app needs free space for the archive; the limit is set under Agents & pairing.
srv.eventlog_desc: Read the Windows event logs, filtered by log, source, level and text.
srv.ps_desc: Runs once as SYSTEM in Windows PowerShell; use the PowerShell button for an interactive session.
srv.health_desc: Failed services, recent errors, top processes, listening ports and time sync in one go.

uf.net_subtitle: Gateways, switches and access points of every customer, with clients, uplinks, firmware, WiFi and events.
uf.acc_subtitle: Doors, lock state, schedules and the access log, with remote unlock.
uf.conn_subtitle: Connect UniFi consoles per environment or customer. Keys are stored encrypted.
uf.dialog_desc: Uses the official UniFi APIs with an API key. Test runs right after saving.
uf.kind_network_desc: A UniFi console or self-hosted Network application. Uses the official Integration API with an API key.
uf.kind_site_manager_desc: All consoles and sites of a UniFi account at once through the cloud API. Handy for many customers; also lets you reach a console's Network API through the cloud.
uf.kind_access_desc: Doors, lock state, schedules and the access log through the Access developer API.
uf.key_note: API keys are stored encrypted and never shown again. A read-only key is enough for monitoring and for Claude's questions; actions (restart, unlock) need a key with write rights and can be switched off per connection.
uf.key_where_network_title: Where to create the API key
uf.key_where_network: In UniFi Network: Settings → Control Plane → Integrations → Create API key (Network 9.0 or newer). The key has the rights of the admin who creates it: use a View Only admin for a read-only key.
uf.key_where_site_manager_title: Where to create the API key
uf.key_where_site_manager: Sign in at unifi.ui.com, open API in the menu and create an API key. Site Manager is read-only, except for the cloud connector to a console.
uf.key_where_access_title: Where to create the API token
uf.key_where_access: In UniFi Access: Settings → General → Advanced → API Token. Pick the permissions: only view rights for a read-only token, add door control for remote unlock. The API listens on port 12445.
uf.tr_direct_hint: This server calls the console itself: same network, a VPN, or a public address.
uf.tr_agent_hint: An agent (server or node) in the customer's network makes the HTTPS call and sends the answer back over its encrypted connection. No port forward needed.
uf.tr_cloud_hint: Reach the console's Network API through the UniFi cloud connector with the Site Manager key (console firmware 5.0.3+, max. 100 requests per minute).
uf.f_env_hint: The customer or Home this connection belongs to.
uf.f_agent_hint: A server or Proxmox node with the agent that can reach the console.
uf.f_url_hint: IP or host name, e.g. https://192.168.1.1. The API path is added automatically; give a full path for a self-hosted Network application.
uf.f_url_access_hint: IP or host name of the console running Access; port 12445 is added when you leave it out.
uf.f_key_keep: Leave empty to keep the current key.
uf.f_ro_hint: No actions from this app or from Claude, only reading. Use it for monitoring.
uf.tls_pin_opt: Pin the console's certificate (recommended for self-signed)
uf.tls_insecure_warn: Without a check, someone on the network could intercept the API key. Pin the certificate instead.
uf.f_fp_hint: Fetch it from the console and compare it with the certificate in the UniFi console if you want to be sure.
uf.f_enabled_hint: Polled every 5 minutes for status and events.
uf.no_cloud: Add a Site Manager connection first.
uf.no_conns_text: Add a UniFi Network console, a Site Manager account or a UniFi Access console.
uf.delete_text: The API key and the event history of this connection are removed. Nothing changes in UniFi itself.
uf.empty_network_text: Connect a console (local Integration API) or a Site Manager account to see all devices, clients and WiFi here.
uf.empty_access_text: Connect a UniFi Access console to see doors and the access log, and to unlock doors remotely.
uf.devices_desc: Offline devices first. Click a device for ports, radios and its clients.
uf.search_devices: Search name, model, IP or MAC
uf.clients_desc: Connected now, live from the console.
uf.search_clients: Search name, MAC, IP or device
uf.cloud_only: Clients and checks need a UniFi Network connection (local or through Site Manager).
uf.wifi_desc: SSIDs per site with their network and VLAN.
uf.no_wifi: No WiFi networks (or this UniFi version doesn't offer them through the API).
uf.wifi_off_warn: All devices on this WiFi network lose their connection.
uf.diag_desc: Why can't a device get on WiFi? Enter its name, MAC or IP.
uf.iso_desc: Is the guest network separated from the LAN? Based on the zone firewall policies.
uf.iso_note: The first matching firewall policy per zone pair decides. Client isolation on the SSID also stops guests from reaching each other.
uf.events_desc: Changes since the previous poll (every 5 min.).
uf.ask_note: Claude uses the same MCP server and tokens; UniFi questions and actions are in the AI activity log like everything else.
uf.ask_n1: Why can't laptop-anna get on the WiFi?
uf.ask_n2: Which access points need a firmware update?
uf.ask_n3: Is the guest network isolated from the LAN?
uf.ask_n4: Which devices went offline today, and was there a WAN failover?
uf.ask_a1: Who opened the server room last night?
uf.ask_a2: Which doors are unlocked right now?
uf.ask_a3: Unlock the front door for the delivery.
uf.cycle_warn: PoE on this port is switched off and on: the device on it restarts.
uf.restart_warn: Clients on this device lose their connection for a few minutes.
uf.restart_gw_warn: This is the gateway: the whole site is offline for a few minutes.
uf.unlock_text: The door unlocks once, like the button in UniFi Access. It shows in the access log under your name.
uf.rule_custom_hint: Stays unlocked for the minutes you choose.
uf.rule_keep_lock_hint: Also outside the schedule, until you reset it.
uf.rule_lock_early_hint: End the current unlock schedule early.
uf.em_lockdown_text: Every door of this console locks and stays locked, also for badges, until you choose Normal.
uf.em_evacuation_text: Every door of this console unlocks and stays unlocked until you choose Normal.
uf.em_normal_text: Doors follow their normal schedules again.
uf.log_desc: Who opened which door, when and how.
